### Why Do Dogs Like to Poop on Dry Leaves?

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/why-dogs-poop-on-dry-leaves/
Published: 2026-11-04 · Updated: 2026-11-06 · Author: Jin

If your dog always stops at a pile of dry leaves on fall walks, that's perfectly normal. The usual explanation: leaf piles hold other dogs' scents for a long time, they're soft enough to squat on comfortably, and less poop ends up on paws. A habit of seeking out the feel of the ground they first pooped on as a puppy plays a part too.

#### 4 reasons dogs love pooping on leaves

Reason | Why it matters |

Lots of scent information | Rain and wind don't wash scent off a leaf pile quickly, so traces left by other dogs linger. It's where your dog catches up on the neighborhood news and leaves a message of their own. |

Soft and comfortable | Squatting is easier than on hard pavement, and less poop gets on paws or the fur around the rear. |

A surface they learned on | Dogs are known to keep preferring the feel of the ground where they first learned to go (grass, dirt, leaves and so on). |

Good cover | Dogs are vulnerable while pooping, so many pick a spot with a little cover, like bushes or a leaf pile. |

Dogs who only go outdoors tend to have especially clear surface preferences. For why some dogs only poop outside, see why some dogs only potty outdoors.

#### Why dogs circle before they poop

Circling is commonly explained as choosing a spot, pressing the leaves flat and checking that nothing dangerous is nearby. A 2013 study that observed 70 dogs made headlines by finding that dogs line their bodies up north–south when Earth's magnetic field is calm, but not every dog does this, so take it as a fun fact.

Kicking leaves with the back legs is common too. The reasons are in why dogs kick their back legs after pooping.

#### What to watch out for in leaf piles

- Ticks: Common in fall leaves and brush. After a walk, check inside the ears, the armpits and between the toes.

- Chestnut burrs, thorns, broken glass: Hard to see under leaves. If your dog licks a paw or limps, take a look.

- Mushrooms, ginkgo nuts, rotting food: Keep the leash short so your dog doesn't eat them.

- Other animals' droppings: Some dogs sniff and then eat them or roll in them.

- Wet leaves: Slippery and prone to mold.

#### How to pick up poop on leaves cleanly

- Double up two bags over your hand and grab it leaves and all. The leaves wrap around the poop, so it's actually cleaner.

- A grabber or a portable scoop makes it even easier.

- Poop can blend in with leaf colors, so take a look at the color and firmness before you pick it up. You can check it against the dog poop condition guide.

This page is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog limps after a walk, or you see ticks or wounds on the skin, talk to your vet.

#### Log fall walks with POOPIEMATE

#### Frequently Asked Questions

Q. Why do dogs want to poop on leaves?

It's commonly explained that leaf piles hold other dogs' scents for a long time, they're soft enough to squat on comfortably, and poop doesn't get on paws. Some dogs also seek out the feel of the ground they got used to as puppies.

Q. Why do dogs circle before pooping?

It's known as a way of choosing a spot and checking the surroundings. One study found dogs line up north–south when conditions are calm, but not every dog does this.

Q. Is it okay to let my dog poop on leaves?

Yes. But leaf piles can hide ticks, chestnut burrs, broken glass, mushrooms and other animals' droppings, so check your dog's paws and body after the walk.

Q. How do I pick up poop on leaves?

Double up two bags over your hand and scoop it up leaves and all for a clean pickup. A grabber or a portable scoop makes it even easier.

### Should You Leave the Heat On for Your Dog When You Go Out?

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/leave-heating-on-for-dog/
Published: 2026-11-04 · Updated: 2026-11-06 · Author: Jin

Rather than switching the heat off completely when you go out, it's usually safer to leave it on away mode or a low temperature. Dogs are commonly said to feel comfortable at an indoor temperature of about 18–22°C (64–72°F), and puppies, senior dogs, small dogs and short-coated dogs feel the cold more. On the other hand, a floor that's too hot can cause low-temperature burns and dehydration, so the key is to give your dog both a warm spot and a cool spot.

#### When you can turn it off, and when to leave it on

Situation | Recommendation |

Well-insulated apartment, healthy adult dog, out for 2–3 hours | Away mode or a very low setting may be enough |

Midwinter with temperatures below freezing, out all day | Leave it on away mode or around 18°C (64°F) |

Puppy, senior, small, short-coated or thin dog | A bit warmer, around 20°C (68°F) |

Dogs with a thick double coat, like a Jindo | A little cool is fine. Just don't let it get too hot |

With the heat off, a poorly insulated home can get quite chilly within a few hours. The problem is that nobody is home to notice if your dog is cold. Away mode often runs only low enough to keep pipes from freezing, so if you'll be gone a long time in midwinter, double-check the temperature setting.

#### Dogs that feel the cold more

- Puppies: They're still not good at regulating body temperature.

- Senior dogs: With less muscle and fat, they get cold easily. Dogs with sore joints stiffen up more in the cold.

- Small or thin dogs: The smaller the body, the faster it loses heat.

- Short or single coats: Dogs with little undercoat, like Chihuahuas, Dachshunds and Poodles, tend to handle cold poorly.

- Dogs who are unwell: If your dog has heart or kidney disease or is recovering from something, ask your vet what temperature is right.

If your dog curls up tight and shivers, only burrows under blankets, or has cold ears and paws, they're cold.

#### Too hot is a problem too

Homes with underfloor heating, the standard in Korea, can get floors hotter than you'd expect. A dog lying on a hot floor for a long time can get low-temperature burns on the belly and around the joints, and the dry indoor air makes them look for water more.

- Don't set the heat too high. If the floor feels hot to your hand, it's hot for your dog too.

- Put down a cushion or mat so there's a layer between the floor and your dog's body.

- Leave doors open so your dog can also get to cool tile or the entryway.

- Set out water in at least two places, filled generously.

- If you use a humidifier, put it where your dog can't knock it over.

#### Beyond the thermostat

- A warm bed: Put a cushion with a blanket a little away from the wall. Windows and the front door let in cold drafts.

- Turn off heating pads and space heaters before you leave: Your dog could chew the cord or get burned lying too close, and there's a fire risk.

- Smart thermostat or home camera: Being able to check the indoor temperature and turn on the heat while you're out is a big relief.

- Walk during the warm hours: In midwinter, keep morning and evening walks short and go out during the day. The walk safety calculator shows how risky it feels hour by hour.

This page is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog keeps shivering, seems low on energy or won't eat, talk to your vet.

#### Stay on top of things while you're out with POOPIEMATE

#### Frequently Asked Questions

Q. Is it okay to turn the heat off when I go out?

For a healthy adult dog alone for a few hours in a well-insulated home, it can be fine. But in midwinter, or for a puppy, senior, small or short-coated dog, it's better to leave it on away mode or a low temperature.

Q. What indoor temperature is right for a dog?

Dogs are commonly said to feel comfortable at about 18–22°C (64–72°F). Dogs who feel the cold can use it a bit warmer, while dogs with a thick double coat, like a Jindo, are fine a little cooler.

Q. Is it bad to turn the heat up too high?

Yes. Underfloor heating makes the floor hot, so lying on it for a long time can cause low-temperature burns, and the air gets dry. Make sure your dog can move to a cooler spot.

Q. Can I leave a heating pad or space heater on when I go out?

Not while your dog is alone. They could chew the cord or get burned lying too close, and there's a fire risk.

### Why Does My Dog Have Diarrhea? When to Watch at Home and When to See a Vet

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/dog-diarrhea-causes/
Published: 2026-10-30 · Updated: 2026-11-06 · Author: Jin

The most common causes of dog diarrhea are minor ones, like a sudden food switch or eating treats or human food. But parasites, viruses, pancreatitis or a swallowed object can also be behind it, so if there's blood, vomiting or your dog is lethargic, it's best to see a vet right away.

#### Common causes of diarrhea in dogs

Cause | When to suspect it |

Sudden food switch | You changed food overnight. The gut needs time to adjust to a new food. |

Treats and human food | Your dog ate a lot of fatty food, milk, or a new treat. |

Stress | Something changed: a move, travel, grooming, boarding, a new family member. |

Parasites | Puppies, or dogs who pick things up and eat them on walks. Giardia, roundworms and others can be the cause. |

Viruses (such as parvo) | Severe diarrhea and vomiting in a puppy who hasn't finished their vaccines. This can be very dangerous. |

Pancreatitis | Vomiting, belly pain and low energy together after eating fatty food. |

Foreign object | Vomiting, diarrhea and loss of appetite after swallowing a toy, bone, plastic bag or similar. |

There are other causes too, such as food allergies, enteritis and medication side effects. Only an exam and tests can tell you the exact cause.

This guide is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog seems tired or unwell, or you're worried about any symptom, talk to your vet.

#### Signs your dog needs a vet right away

- Bloody diarrhea, or black, sticky poop

- Vomiting too, or can't even keep water down

- Limp and low on energy, or in pain when you touch the belly

- Diarrhea in a puppy who hasn't finished their vaccines, a senior dog, or a dog with an existing condition

- Diarrhea that lasts more than a day

- You think they swallowed something

Puppies and small dogs can get dehydrated quickly, so act sooner with them.

#### What to try at home for mild diarrhea

If it's just once or twice and your dog is eating and playing normally, many owners watch for about a day.

- Plenty of water: make sure clean water is available at all times.

- Stop treats and human food: start by cutting out any new treat.

- Go back to the usual food: if you switched recently, return to the old food, and when you do switch, go slowly using the 7–10 day schedule in How to get healthy, firm dog poop.

- Keep a log: note how many times your dog went and what the color and texture looked like. Compare them with the dog poop color and texture chart.

- No human medicine: human anti-diarrhea medicine can be dangerous for dogs. Only use what your vet prescribes.

If yellow diarrhea or gray poop keeps coming, also see why dog poop turns yellow or gray.

#### Spot changes early with POOPIEMATE

#### Frequently Asked Questions

Q. My dog had diarrhea once. Do I need a vet?

If it's once or twice and your dog is eating and playing normally, many owners watch for about a day. If there's blood, vomiting or lethargy, or it lasts more than a day, see a vet.

Q. What's the most common cause of diarrhea in dogs?

Minor causes are common, like a sudden food switch, eating treats or human food, or stress. It can also be parasites, a virus or pancreatitis, so if it keeps going, your dog needs tests.

Q. Should I stop feeding my dog when they have diarrhea?

Fasting your dog for a long time on your own isn't recommended. Puppies and small dogs in particular can develop low blood sugar and dehydration. Ask your vet how to feed them.

Q. Can I give my dog human anti-diarrhea medicine?

Human medicine can be dangerous for dogs. Only use medicine your vet prescribes.

Q. My puppy has diarrhea and is vomiting.

If your puppy hasn't finished their vaccines, it could be a virus such as parvo, so go to the vet right away.

### Dog Constipation: Causes, How to Help at Home, and When to See a Vet

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/dog-constipation-causes/
Published: 2026-10-30 · Updated: 2026-11-06 · Author: Jin

Dog constipation often happens when a dog drinks too little water, doesn't get enough exercise, or holds their poop for too long. If your dog hasn't pooped in more than two days, or strains without anything coming out and seems in pain, talk to your vet.

#### Signs of constipation in dogs

- Hard, small poop, or round pellets like rabbit droppings

- Holding the squat and straining for a long time, with little or nothing coming out

- No poop for more than a day

- A little mucus or blood on the poop

One thing to watch for: long straining isn't always constipation. It can also mean your dog can't pee (a urinary blockage). Always check that urine is coming out too.

#### Common causes of dog constipation

Cause | What happens |

Not enough water | When a dog drinks little, the gut pulls more water out of the poop and it turns hard. Pay extra attention if your dog eats only dry kibble. |

Not enough exercise | Walking and running get the gut moving too. Fewer walks can mean slower poops. |

Too little or too much fiber | Too little fiber, or a sudden jump to a lot, can both upset the gut. |

Bones and foreign objects | Eating a lot of bone tends to make white, hard poop. Hair or bits of toys can also cause a blockage. |

Holding it | When an outdoor-only dog misses walks and holds it, poop sits in the gut for a long time. See Why outdoor-only dogs shouldn't hold it. |

Old age | As dogs age, the gut slows down and they move less. |

Anal glands and pain | Full anal glands, or a sore rear end or joints, can make a dog avoid the squatting position altogether. |

Medication and illness | Some medications, prostate problems, or nerve and hormone conditions can also be the cause. |

This guide is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog seems tired or unwell, or you're worried about any symptom, talk to your vet.

#### How to help a constipated dog at home

- Get them drinking more: put water bowls in several places, and after checking with your vet, try mixing in some wet food.

- Walk more: more time on their feet keeps the gut moving. A walk a little while after a meal works well.

- Give more potty chances: if your dog only goes outside, head out several times a day.

- Cut back on bones and chews: if hard poop keeps happening, reduce bone treats.

- Fiber, with your vet: adding fiber such as pumpkin is a commonly known approach, but the right amount differs for every dog, so ask your vet first.

- No human laxatives: human enemas and laxatives can be dangerous for dogs.

#### Signs your dog needs a vet right away

- No poop for more than two days

- Whining or crying in pain while straining

- Vomiting, no appetite, or a bloated, painful belly

- You think they swallowed a foreign object or a bone

- They're also struggling to pee (this is even more urgent)

For what's a normal count, see how often a dog should poop, and for texture, check the dog poop color and texture chart.

#### Spot changes early with POOPIEMATE

#### Frequently Asked Questions

Q. Is it dangerous if my dog hasn't pooped for a few days?

A day can happen, but if your dog goes more than two days without pooping, strains in pain, or is vomiting or off their food, talk to your vet.

Q. Are there foods that help dog constipation?

Making sure your dog drinks enough water comes first. Fiber such as pumpkin is often mentioned, but the right amount differs for every dog, so check with your vet.

Q. My dog's poop is white and hard.

This is common on diets high in bone or calcium. If it keeps happening, cut back on bone treats, and talk to your vet if there are signs of constipation.

Q. I thought my dog was constipated, but no urine is coming out.

The straining may be a urinary blockage. If your dog can't pee, go to the vet right away.

### How to Get the Perfect Poop: From Switching Dog Food to the 10% Treat Rule

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/how-to-get-golden-poop/
Published: 2026-10-30 · Updated: 2026-11-06 · Author: Jin

Healthy, firm dog poop comes from the basics, not a secret trick. Feed the same amount at set times; when you change food, don't switch overnight but mix it into the old food little by little over 7 to 10 days; give plenty of water and walks; and keep treats under 10% of daily calories. That's the core of it.

#### What is "the perfect poop"?

In Korea, dog owners call ideal stool "golden poop": chocolate brown, moist, but firm enough to hold its shape when you pick it up. In this guide we call it the perfect poop. For the full picture, see the dog poop color and texture chart.

#### 1. Set mealtimes, set amounts

When mealtimes are regular, the gut's rhythm becomes regular too, and potty times get easier to predict. Splitting food into meals, such as 2 a day (3 to 4 for puppies), often helps with poop more than free-feeding. Start from the amount recommended on the food bag and adjust as you watch your dog's weight. Overeating makes poop softer and bigger.

#### 2. Switch dog food gradually over 7 to 10 days

Changing food overnight easily leads to diarrhea. The commonly recommended method is to raise the share of new food a little at a time, like this.

Days | Old food | New food |

Days 1–2 | 75% | 25% |

Days 3–4 | 50% | 50% |

Days 5–6 | 25% | 75% |

Day 7 onward | 0% | 100% |

For dogs with sensitive stomachs, it's fine to add a day to each step and take more than 10 days. If poop turns soft partway through, go back one step.

#### 3. Water and walks

- Make sure clean water is available at all times. Too little water makes poop hard.

- The gut moves while your dog walks. Regular walks make for regular poops.

- Make sure an outdoor-only dog gets enough chances to go. See Why outdoor-only dogs shouldn't hold it.

#### 4. Keep treats under 10% of daily calories

This is the well-known "10% rule." Too many treats throw off nutritional balance and tend to make poop soft. Human food, especially fatty food, can cause diarrhea and pancreatitis, so it's best avoided. Introduce new treats one at a time, starting small.

#### 5. Probiotics and fiber as extras

Dog probiotics and fiber are known to possibly help gut health. But not every dog needs them, and they're an extra to add once the basics (food, water, walks) are steady. If your dog has a health condition or takes medication, check with your vet first.

#### 6. A log shows you the cause

When poop suddenly turns soft or hard, a log lets you find what changed a few days earlier. A new treat, a food switch, or a change in walks are common causes. If soft poop keeps coming, see Why dogs get diarrhea; if hard poop keeps coming, see Dog constipation causes.

This guide is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog seems tired or unwell, or you're worried about any symptom, talk to your vet.

#### Spot changes early with POOPIEMATE

#### Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How many days should it take to switch dog food?

The common advice is to raise the share of new food step by step to 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% over 7 to 10 days. If your dog has a sensitive stomach, going even slower is fine.

Q. How many treats can I give my dog?

A commonly cited guideline is to keep treats under 10% of your dog's daily calories. Cut back the regular food a little to make up for treats.

Q. Will probiotics give my dog perfect poop?

They're known to possibly help, but not every dog needs them. Food, water and walks come first, and if your dog has a health condition, check with your vet.

Q. My dog's poop suddenly got soft. What should I check first?

First check for a recent food switch, a new treat, human food or stress. If it lasts more than a day, or there's blood or vomiting, see a vet.

### Yellow or Gray Dog Poop: What It Means and When to See a Vet

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/yellow-gray-dog-poop/
Published: 2026-10-30 · Updated: 2026-11-06 · Author: Jin

Yellow dog poop is often down to food or poop moving through the gut too fast, while gray or white poo can come from a bone-heavy diet or a bile or pancreas problem. If it happens once, keep an eye on it, but if it lasts a few days, looks greasy, or comes with diarrhea or vomiting, talk to your vet.

#### Why is healthy dog poop brown?

Bile made in the liver changes as it moves through the gut, and that's what turns poop brown. So when bile doesn't mix in well, poop moves through too fast, or food isn't digested properly, the color can change.

#### Why dog poop turns yellow

Cause | What happens |

Food and treats | Ingredients or coloring in the food, or yellow treats (pumpkin, sweet potato and so on), can make poop look yellow. |

Fast gut transit | When poop moves through the gut too fast, bile doesn't have time to turn brown, so it can come out yellow. It often shows up with soft stools or diarrhea. |

Liver or bile duct problems | If yellow poop comes with yellowing eyes or gums, or low energy, the liver or gallbladder may need a check. |

Giardia and other parasites | Suspect this when soft, yellow poop with mucus keeps coming back. A stool test confirms it. |

#### Why dog poop turns gray or white

Cause | What happens |

A diet high in bone or calcium | A raw diet or lots of bone treats can produce white poop that crumbles like chalk. Constipation often comes with it. |

Not enough bile | When bile doesn't reach the gut properly, poop can turn pale gray or clay-colored. |

Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI) | Without enough digestive enzymes, poop comes out grayish, greasy and large in volume, and a dog can lose weight even while eating well. |

Fatty stool | When fat isn't digested, poop can come out gray, shiny and very smelly. |

White, rice-like bits aren't a poop color. They can be worms, so have your vet run a test.

This guide is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog seems tired or unwell, or you're worried about any symptom, talk to your vet.

#### When to see a vet

- Go right away: yellow poop with yellowing eyes, gums or skin; vomiting or lethargy along with it; any blood

- Call soon: gray or clay-colored poop that keeps coming; greasy, large poops together with weight loss

- Watch a few days, then call: soft, yellow poop that lasts more than 2 to 3 days; white poop and constipation that keep coming back

To check other colors (black, green, bloody) all in one place, use the dog poop color chart. If there's diarrhea too, also see Why dogs get diarrhea.

#### Spot changes early with POOPIEMATE

#### Frequently Asked Questions

Q. My dog's poop is yellow. Is that okay?

If it's a one-off and your dog is eating and playing normally, it may just be the food or treats. If it lasts a few days, comes with diarrhea or vomiting, or the eyes or gums turn yellow, talk to your vet.

Q. What does gray dog poop mean?

It can mean bile isn't mixing in well, or the pancreas isn't making enough digestive enzymes. If it looks greasy or keeps happening, talk to your vet.

Q. My dog's poop is white and crumbly.

This is common on diets high in bone or calcium. Constipation often comes with it, so cut back on bones and check with your vet.

Q. My dog has yellow diarrhea with mucus.

The gut may be irritated, or it could be a parasite such as giardia. If it keeps coming back, get a stool test.

### Kibble, Cooked or Raw: Which Diet Gives the Best Dog Poop?

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/kibble-vs-cooked-vs-raw-poop/
Published: 2026-10-30 · Updated: 2026-11-06 · Author: Jin

Poop amount, smell and firmness can change from one diet to another, but no single diet gives every dog the "best" poop. The right diet for your dog is the one they eat well, that keeps their poop consistently healthy, and that keeps their weight and energy steady.

#### How poop can differ by diet (general tendencies)

Diet | Amount | Smell | Firmness |

Dry kibble | Varies a lot with ingredients and fiber. High-fiber food tends to mean more poop. | Varies by food. | Usually fairly consistent. Can get hard if your dog doesn't drink enough water. |

Cooked (home-cooked or fresh-cooked) | Easily digested ingredients can mean less poop; lots of vegetables can mean more. | Depends on the ingredients. | More moisture, so it can be a little softer. |

Raw | Often said to be smaller. | Often said to smell less. | Tends to be firm. With a lot of bone, it can turn white and crumbly. |

These are only commonly reported tendencies. Even on the same diet, poop can vary widely with the ingredients, the ratios and your dog's own body. Less poop isn't automatically better, either.

#### Pros and cons of each diet

Diet | Pros | Watch out for |

Dry kibble | Easy to find a complete, nutritionally balanced food, and easy to store and serve. | Low in moisture, so make sure your dog drinks plenty of water. |

Cooked | High in moisture, and many dogs love it. | Home-cooked meals are hard to balance nutritionally. It's best to go over recipes with your vet. |

Raw | Many dogs love it. | Bacterial hygiene risks, nutritional balance, and constipation or foreign-body risks from bones. |

#### Raw feeding: don't skip the hygiene

Uncooked meat can carry bacteria such as Salmonella. Dogs can shed bacteria in their poop even without symptoms, so homes with babies, older adults or anyone with a weakened immune system need to be extra careful.

- Wash your hands, cutting boards and bowls right after preparing it.

- Don't leave uneaten raw food sitting out.

- Pick up poop right away and wash your hands afterward.

- If you feed bones, check the size and amount with your vet.

#### What to watch when switching diets

- Whatever the diet, don't switch overnight. Mix the new food into the old one a little at a time over 7 to 10 days. The mixing chart is in how to help your dog have healthy poop.

- Log your dog's poop every day during the switch. You can check firmness and color with the dog poop color and firmness chart.

- If soft poop keeps coming, go back one step. If diarrhea lasts more than a day, read causes of diarrhea in dogs and see your vet.

- If white, hard poop keeps showing up, suspect the bone ratio. Also see why dog poop turns yellow or gray.

#### Bottom line: the right answer is different for every dog

When choosing a diet, look beyond poop to weight, coat, energy, age and any health conditions. Puppies, seniors and dogs with health conditions in particular should see a vet before changing diets.

This article is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog seems low on energy or has symptoms that worry you, talk to your vet.

#### Spot changes early with POOPIEMATE

#### Frequently Asked Questions

Q. Which gives the best poop: kibble, cooked or raw?

There's no answer that fits every dog. The right diet is the one your dog eats well, that keeps their poop consistently healthy, and that keeps their weight and energy steady.

Q. My dog's poop comes out white on a raw diet.

A high bone or calcium ratio can make poop white and crumbly. It can easily lead to constipation, so talk to your vet about the bone ratio.

Q. My dog's poop got soft after starting cooked food.

The switch may have been too fast, or the food may be high in moisture or fat. Switch more slowly, and if it stays soft for more than a day, talk to your vet.

Q. Is raw feeding dangerous?

Uncooked meat can carry bacteria, so careful hygiene is a must. There are also nutritional-balance and bone-related risks, so it's best to talk to your vet before starting.

### How Often Do Puppies Poop and Pee? By Age and Dog Size

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/puppy-potty-count-by-size/
Published: 2026-10-30 · Updated: 2026-11-06 · Author: Jin

Puppies usually poop 3 to 5 times a day and pee far more often than that. How much and how often they eat matters more than their size, and once they're adults, 1 to 2 poops a day is common for dogs of any size.

#### Daily potty count by age (common guidelines)

Age | Poops per day | How long they can hold pee |

2–3 months | About 4 to 5. They often go after every meal. | About 2 to 4 hours |

4–6 months | About 3 to 4 | About 4 to 6 hours |

7–12 months | About 2 to 3 | Gradually getting closer to an adult. |

Adult | 1 to 2 (up to 3) | Give them a chance at least once every 6 to 8 hours |

A common rule of thumb is that puppies can hold their pee for "their age in months + 1 hour." At 3 months, that's about 4 hours. But this is closer to a maximum than a target, so taking a puppy out more often than that also helps with potty training. Adult guidelines are in how often a dog should poop and potty intervals.

#### When puppies usually need to go

- Right after waking up

- 10 to 30 minutes after eating

- Right after an exciting play session

- After drinking a lot of water

Take them to their potty spot at these moments and praise them when they go. Potty training goes much faster.

#### Potty count by dog size

Size | Poop | Pee | Notes |

Small dogs | 1 to 2 a day is common. | Small bladders, so they tend to go more often. | Small amounts make soft stools and diarrhea easy to miss. Dehydration also sets in quickly. |

Medium dogs | 1 to 2 a day is common. | Average | Varies a lot with activity level. |

Large dogs | 1 to 2 a day is common. | A lot at once. | They eat more, so they poop more. |

Rather than size changing the count dramatically, how much they eat, how many meals they get, and how active they are matter more. That's why knowing your own dog's usual count matters more than an average. If your dog only goes on walks, also see how to track potty for a dog who only goes outside.

#### When to worry

- See a vet now: a puppy with both diarrhea and vomiting (hurry even more if they haven't finished their vaccinations), bloody stool, or a limp, listless puppy

- See a vet now: straining to pee with nothing coming out

- Talk to your vet: no poop for more than a day, or a sudden big rise or drop in how often they pee

- Talk to your vet: poop firmness or color that's been off for several days. Check it with the dog poop color and firmness chart.

This article is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog seems low on energy or has symptoms that worry you, talk to your vet.

#### Spot changes early with POOPIEMATE

#### Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How many times a day do puppies poop?

Usually about 3 to 5 times a day, more often than adult dogs. They eat more meals and digest quickly, so they often go soon after eating.

Q. How many hours can a puppy hold their pee?

A common rule is "their age in months + 1 hour." At 3 months that's about 4 hours, but it's closer to a maximum, so take them out more often.

Q. Do small dogs go more often than large dogs?

Poop count depends more on how much and how often they eat than on size, so most adult dogs go 1 to 2 times a day. Small dogs do tend to pee more often.

Q. My puppy hasn't pooped all day.

They may be eating less, or their surroundings may have changed. If they strain and seem uncomfortable, or are vomiting or losing their appetite, talk to your vet.

### Why Do Dogs Only Potty Outside and Not at Home?

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/dog-outdoor-potty-why/
Published: 2026-10-30 · Updated: 2026-11-14 · Author: Jin

Dogs that only go outside are combining an instinct to keep where they sleep and eat clean, a habit of marking territory with scent, and a routine of going on walks that has become second nature. It's not strange at all. It's very natural behavior.

#### 4 reasons dogs only potty outside

Reason | What it means |

Keeping the den clean | Dogs are known to have an instinct to go far from where they sleep and eat. If they see the whole home as "my den," they try to hold it indoors. |

Scent marking | Pee and poop carry scent information unique to each dog. Sniffing another dog's scent on a walk and going on top of it is a kind of greeting and a mark. |

A set habit | If they went on walks and got praised for it from puppyhood, they learn "potty = outside." Independent-minded dogs, like Jindo mixes (a Korean breed known for being clean and independent), tend to have an especially strong habit. |

Outside just feels better | Dirt and grass feel familiar underfoot, and all the smells can help get the gut moving. Walking itself also gets the bowels going. |

#### Is it a problem that they won't go at home?

Going only outside isn't a problem in itself. But on days you can't walk because of rain, storms or a cold snap, or when you get home late, your dog has to hold it for a long time. Holding it for long stretches again and again can put strain on the bladder and bowels. More on this in why outdoor-only dogs shouldn't hold it.

On the other hand, if a dog who used to go at home suddenly refuses to go indoors and only wants to go outside, the pad may have moved, or they may have been scolded after an accident at home.

#### How to teach indoor potty as a backup

Teaching an outdoor-only dog to use an indoor spot as a "backup" makes bad-weather days much easier. Think of it as giving them one more option, not forcing a change.

- Bring the outdoor smell inside: put a tissue or some grass with their pee on it from a walk onto the pad, and they're more likely to feel "this is a bathroom too."

- Match the feel: try something that feels like outside, such as an artificial grass pad or a dirt-textured mat.

- Get the timing right: take them to the pad when they're likely to go, like right after waking up or a little after eating.

- Start near the door or balcony: make a spot "close to outside" the bathroom first, rather than the middle of the living room.

- Praise big when they succeed: give a treat and praise the moment they go or right after. Don't scold accidents; just clean up quietly.

It often takes several weeks. The most important thing is not to rush.

This article is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog hasn't been able to go for a long time, or strains without anything coming out, talk to your vet.

#### Walk time is potty time

For outdoor-only dogs, every walk is a potty chance. If your family takes turns walking, it matters that everyone knows "when they last went." On days the weather looks bad, check whether it's okay to go out first with the dog walk safety index.

#### Never miss a potty with the POOPIEMATE Poopie Gauge

#### More on outdoor-only pottying

- Why do Jindos insist on pottying outside?

- Why do big dogs only potty outside?

- Why outdoor-only dogs shouldn't hold it

- Jindo mix potty training

- Tracking potty for an outdoor-only dog

#### Frequently Asked Questions

Q. Is it strange that my dog only goes outside?

No. It's natural behavior that combines the instinct to keep where they sleep clean, scent marking, and walk habits.

Q. Can an outdoor-only dog learn to go indoors?

Yes. Use a pad with outdoor scent on it or artificial grass, take them there when they're likely to go, and praise them when they succeed. It often takes several weeks.

Q. What should I do on days we can't go for a walk?

Step outside the door even briefly to give them a potty chance, or use an indoor pad as a backup. If they can't go for more than a day and seem uncomfortable, talk to your vet.

Q. My dog used to go at home but suddenly only goes outside.

It may be because the pad moved or they were scolded after an accident. If how often they pee or the color has changed, it could be a health issue, so talk to your vet.

### Is It Bad for Dogs to Hold Their Pee and Poop? Risks and Tips

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/outdoor-potty-holding-risks/
Published: 2026-10-30 · Updated: 2026-11-14 · Author: Jin

Dogs that only go outside simply hold it when they can't get a walk. Now and then is fine, but if long holds keep happening, they can lead to problems like bladder infections, urinary stones and constipation, so it's best to give them several potty chances a day.

#### Why holding it is hard on the body

Pee flushes waste and bacteria out of the body. When it sits for a long time, bacteria can multiply more easily, and minerals in the urine have more time to clump together. Poop also loses water and gets harder the longer it stays in the bowel.

#### Problems that can come from holding it too long

Problem | How it happens | Signs to look for |

Urinary tract infection / bladder infection | Bacteria can multiply in urine that sits. | Trying to go often but only a little comes out, blood in the urine, a change in smell |

Urinary stones | Minerals in concentrated urine can form crystals or stones. Drinking little water makes this more likely. | Straining with nothing coming out, blood in the urine, signs of pain |

Constipation / impacted stool | Poop that stays in the bowel a long time can get hard. | Small, hard poops, straining for a long time |

Stretched bladder | Holding it for very long stretches again and again can strain the bladder muscle. | Not emptying fully, leaking urine |

Strain on the kidneys | If the urinary tract gets blocked or an infection spreads upward, it can affect the kidneys too. | Low energy, vomiting, drinking unusually large amounts of water |

This table is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog strains and not a single drop of urine comes out, the urethra may be blocked, so go to the vet right away. Blood in the urine, vomiting or a limp, listless dog also need a vet right away.

#### How many hours can a dog hold it? (common guidelines)

Age / condition | Common guideline | Notes |

Puppy | About their age in months + 1 hour | Around 4 hours at 3 months. Taking them out more often is still better. |

Adult | A chance at least once every 6 to 8 hours | About 3 to 5 potty chances a day is the common advice. |

Senior or dogs with health conditions | Shorter than adults | Bladder control can weaken, so let them out more often. |

Dogs may hold it longer overnight while sleeping, but it's best to avoid a run of days with no chance to go for more than 8 hours during the day. To find your dog's usual interval from your logs, see how often a dog should poop and potty intervals.

#### What to do on rainy, stormy or freezing days

- Go out, even briefly: you don't need a long walk. Stepping out front just to do their business is enough. Have a raincoat and a towel for paws ready.

- Don't push it on dangerous days: on dangerous days like typhoons, heavy rain or cold-wave warnings, check the dog walk safety index first, and use sheltered spots like under an awning or a parking garage entrance.

- Use an indoor pad as backup: teaching your dog to use an indoor pad ahead of time makes these days much less stressful. How to do it is in why do dogs only potty outside?.

- Don't cut back on water: limiting water so they pee less actually makes urinary problems more likely.

#### Never miss a potty with the POOPIEMATE Poopie Gauge

#### More on outdoor-only pottying

- Why do Jindos insist on pottying outside?

- Why do big dogs only potty outside?

- Why do dogs only potty outside?

- Jindo mix potty training

- Tracking potty for an outdoor-only dog

#### Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How many hours can a dog hold their pee?

The common guideline is about their age in months + 1 hour for puppies, and a chance at least once every 6 to 8 hours for adults. Every dog is different, so it helps to know your dog's usual interval from your logs.

Q. My outdoor-only dog hasn't gone all day. Is that okay?

Dogs often hold it because of the weather, but holding it a long time is hard on the body. Take them out even briefly, and if they strain and nothing comes out, go to the vet right away.

Q. What illnesses can holding pee cause?

It can make urinary tract infections, bladder infections and urinary stones more likely, and in serious cases it can strain the kidneys. Poop can harden and lead to constipation.

Q. Can I skip the walk on a rainy day?

You can skip the long walk, but still give them a potty chance. You can step out front briefly just to do their business, or use an indoor pad as a backup.

### Why Do Dogs Kick After Pooping? Should You Stop It?

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/why-dogs-kick-after-pooping/
Published: 2026-10-30 · Updated: 2026-11-06 · Author: Jin

When a dog kicks the ground with their back legs after pooping, they aren't trying to cover it. It's known as a marking behavior that leaves an "I was here" message through paw scent and scratch marks. It's completely natural, so in most cases there's no need to stop it.

#### 3 reasons dogs kick after pooping

Reason | Explanation |

Paw scent marking | Dogs have sweat glands in their paw pads. Kicking the ground is thought to rub that paw scent in and leave it alongside the smell of the poop. |

A visible mark | The scratch marks and scattered dirt and grass are said to act as a sign that "someone was here." It's a signal to other dogs that come by to sniff. |

Relief and good feelings | Some dogs kick out of sheer excitement after a good poop, the way they shake themselves off. |

Wild canids like wolves are also known to scratch the ground in a similar way. That's why many see it as an instinct passed down over a very long time. Some dogs scratch the air or the floor after going on a pad at home. It's the same behavior, so there's nothing to worry about.

People often think dogs do this "to cover their poop," but actually covering it is rare. Unlike cats, many dogs kick at a spot a little away from the poop.

#### Which dogs kick more often?

- It's often said to be more common in unneutered males, but females and neutered dogs do it too.

- Outdoor-only dogs do it more often on walks, where there's lots of scent information. Why dogs go only outside is covered in why do dogs only potty outside?.

- Some dogs kick after peeing too. It's the same marking behavior.

- Plenty of dogs never kick at all. That's not strange either.

#### Should you stop it?

In most cases, no. For dogs it's a natural way of expressing themselves. But in these situations, gently redirect them.

- When they're tearing up someone else's flower bed or lawn: as soon as they finish, shorten the leash and move a few steps away.

- When dirt or sand is flying at people: pick a potty spot away from the path.

- On glass, thorns or hot ground: they can hurt their paw pads. On summer afternoons, check the asphalt ahead of time with the dog walk safety index.

#### When to talk to a vet

- They limp or keep licking their paw pads after kicking

- They drag their bottom on the floor (scooting) or keep licking their rear (it could be an anal gland problem)

- Their poop looks different from usual. Check it with the dog poop color and firmness chart.

This article is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog seems low on energy or has symptoms that worry you, talk to your vet.

#### Spot changes early with POOPIEMATE

#### Frequently Asked Questions

Q. Why do dogs kick the ground with their back legs after pooping?

It's known as a marking behavior that leaves their trace through paw sweat-gland scent and scratch marks. Some dogs also kick because they feel good after a good poop.

Q. Are they kicking to cover their poop?

Mostly not. Covering the poop is rare; it's closer to a marking behavior that leaves scent and scratch marks.

Q. Should I stop my dog from kicking after pooping?

It's natural behavior, so in most cases you don't need to stop it. Only gently redirect them with the leash when they're tearing up someone's flower bed or the ground is unsafe.

Q. My dog never kicks. Is that okay?

Yes. Lots of dogs don't kick. It depends on personality and habit.

### Dog Poop Color Chart: What Healthy Dog Poop Looks Like and What Each Color Means

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/poop-condition-guide/
Published: 2026-08-27 · Updated: 2026-11-06 · Author: Jin

Healthy dog poop is usually chocolate brown and firm enough to hold its shape when you pick it up. If the color or texture stays different from normal for a few days, talk to your vet.

#### What healthy dog poop looks like

- Color: chocolate brown

- Texture: moist but holds its shape, and leaves little or no mark on the ground

- Shape: log-shaped, with slight segments

- How often: adult dogs commonly go 1 to 2 times a day. More in how often a dog should poop.

#### Dog poop texture: what it may mean

Texture | What it may mean (common guidelines) |

Very hard and small | Possible constipation. Check water intake and activity. |

Firm and well-formed (Good) | Often described as healthy. |

Soft | May point to indigestion, stress or a change in food or treats. |

Fully liquid (diarrhea) | Risk of dehydration. See a vet if it lasts more than a day or your dog seems weak. |

With mucus | The gut may be irritated. See a vet if it keeps happening. |

#### Dog stool score chart (fecal score 1 to 7)

Vets often rate dog poop on a 1 to 7 fecal score (stool score) scale. A score of 2 is usually called ideal, and 3 is still in the normal range.

Score | What it looks like | What it may mean |

1: Hard pellets | Dry, hard pieces. Your dog strains to pass them. | Sign of constipation |

2: Firm and well-formed | Clear shape and firm. It keeps its shape when you pick it up. | Ideal |

3: Moist log | Moist surface. Leaves a little mark when you pick it up. | Normal range |

4: Soft pile | Loses its shape and leaves residue on the ground. | Soft stool |

5: Shapeless pile | Some form, but hard to pick up. | Soft stool |

6: Mushy diarrhea | Has texture but no shape. | Diarrhea |

7: Watery diarrhea | Spreads like water, no shape at all. | Diarrhea |

#### Dog poop color chart

Color | What it may mean (common guidelines) |

Brown (chocolate) | Often described as normal. |

Yellow or orange | Can follow a food change or fast digestion. If it keeps happening, the liver or gallbladder may need a check. |

Green | Lots of grass or food coloring. See a vet if it lasts a few days. |

Black, sticky and tar-like | Can be a sign of bleeding in the stomach or small intestine. Go to the vet right away. |

Dark red, or bright red blood (bloody stool) | Can mean bleeding in the gut or near the rear. See a vet right away. |

Gray or white | Can point to a bile or pancreas problem, especially if it looks greasy. A vet visit is recommended. |

White, rice-like bits | Possible worms. Ask your vet for a test. |

These tables are general reference information, not a diagnosis. If you see a warning sign, or your dog is tired and not eating, always check with your vet.

#### What does the color of diarrhea tell you?

Check the color of diarrhea too. If it's one or two soft brown or yellow stools and your dog is eating and playing normally, many owners watch for about a day. Black or bloody diarrhea, diarrhea that lasts more than a day, or diarrhea with vomiting needs a vet right away.

#### Why it helps to log it with POOPIEMATE

#### FAQ

Q. What does healthy dog poop look like?

Chocolate brown, moist but firm enough to hold its shape when you pick it up.

Q. Is gray or white dog poop a problem?

Gray or white poop can point to a bile or pancreas problem, so a vet visit is recommended. If you see white, rice-like bits, ask for a worm test.

Q. What should I do if I see bloody or black poop?

Bloody poop or sticky black poop can be a sign of bleeding, so contact your vet right away.

Q. My dog had diarrhea once. Do I need a vet?

If it's once or twice and your dog is eating and playing normally, many owners watch for about a day. If it lasts more than a day, has blood, or comes with vomiting, see a vet.

### How Often Should a Dog Poop? Daily Potty Count and Intervals

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/potty-interval/
Published: 2026-08-27 · Updated: 2026-10-28 · Author: Jin

Adult dogs commonly poop 1 to 2 times a day, but age, food and activity make a big difference. Knowing your own dog's usual count and rhythm matters more than any average.

#### How many times a day dogs poop, by age (common guidelines)

Age | Poops per day | Notes |

Puppy (up to about 6 months) | About 3 to 5 | More meals and fast digestion, so they often go soon after eating. |

Adult | 1 to 2 (up to 3) | Depends on food and walks. If it's regular, that's normal for your dog. |

Senior | 1 to 2 | Slower digestion makes constipation more likely. |

This page is general reference information and does not replace an individual diagnosis. If you're worried about your dog's health, talk to your vet.

#### What is a potty interval?

The potty interval is the time between one poop and the next. For an adult dog who goes twice a day, that's usually around half a day. Dogs often go after meals, after waking up and on walks, so a steady daily routine makes the interval steady too.

#### What affects how often a dog poops

- Age and size

- Type and amount of food, meals per day, treats

- Activity and number of walks (for outdoor-only dogs, every walk is a potty chance)

- Stress and changes like moving or travel

- Health (gut conditions, digestive issues and so on)

#### When to talk to a vet

- No poop for more than a day, with straining or a sore belly (possible constipation or a blockage)

- A sudden jump in how often they go, with soft stools that keep coming (possible diarrhea or illness)

- Color or texture changes too. See what poop color means.

An accurate log makes it much easier to explain "when it changed."

#### Learn your dog's own rhythm with POOPIEMATE

#### FAQ

Q. How many times a day should a dog poop?

Adult dogs commonly go 1 to 2 times a day, and puppies more often, about 3 to 5 times. Age, food and activity vary a lot, so knowing your dog's usual count matters more.

Q. Is it okay if my dog doesn't poop for a day?

A day can happen, but if it goes longer and your dog strains or seems uncomfortable, talk to your vet.

Q. Should I see a vet if the potty interval suddenly changes?

If the interval gets much longer or shorter than usual and it lasts a few days, talk to your vet.

### How to Track Potty for a Dog Who Only Goes Outside

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/outdoor-potty-dog-tracking/
Published: 2026-08-27 · Updated: 2026-11-14 · Author: Jin

With dogs who only go outside, often only the person who took the walk knows if they went. The key habit is logging right after the walk and sharing it with your family.

#### Common problems with outdoor-only dogs

- There's no way to check at home whether they went.

- When the walker changes from day to day, the rest of the family has no idea if the dog went.

- You end up guessing how long it's been since the last potty.

#### Tips

- Log it during the walk or right after you get back, before you forget

- Note whether they went (yes or no) and the time

- Make sure the whole family can see the same log in real time

### Jindo Mix Potty Training: Why Does It Feel So Hard?

Published: 2026-08-27 · Updated: 2026-11-14 · Author: Jin

Jindo mixes aren't especially untrainable. They're smart and independent, so a steady routine and a good log matter more for them.

#### Commonly known Jindo mix traits

- Smart and quick to learn, but independent. Without repetition, they tend to decide for themselves what to do

- Very alert, so they can be sensitive to new places and people

- Often said to prefer going potty outside

#### Potty training basics

- Repeat at the same time and in the same place every day

- Praise and reward right away when they get it right

- After an accident, focus on setting them up to succeed next time instead of scolding

#### The tracking problem with dogs who prefer going outside

If your dog prefers to go outside, it's hard to tell at home whether they went, and only the person who took the walk knows. We cover this in more detail in How to track potty for a dog who only goes outside.

### What Is a Dog Walk Safety Index? Is It Safe to Walk Today?

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/walk-safety-index/
Published: 2026-08-27 · Updated: 2026-10-28 · Author: Jin

It's a score that shows how safe today's walk is on a 1 to 5 scale. It combines the feels-like temperature and chance of rain with your dog's size, age and coat. Lower means safer. Higher means you should be more careful.

#### Why it's worth checking

In summer, the big risks are paw burns from hot asphalt and heatstroke. In winter, it's hypothermia. Your dog may feel heat and cold differently than you do, so it helps to look at feels-like temperature and UV too.

#### Quick checks you can do right now

- The 5-second hand test: Press the back of your hand on the asphalt for 5 seconds. If it feels hot to you, it can be even riskier for your dog's paws.

- In summer, early morning or after sunset is safest, when temperatures and UV are lower.

- In winter, try to skip very windy times, when the feels-like temperature drops a lot.

#### What POOPIEMATE calculates for you

#### FAQ

Q. How is walk safety calculated?

It combines the feels-like temperature and chance of rain with your dog's size, age, coat and body condition, then rates it on a 1 to 5 scale. A higher number means more caution is needed. You also get suggested safe walk times for today and tomorrow.

Q. What's the best time to walk a dog in summer?

Early morning or after sunset is usually safest, when temperatures and UV are lower. It's best to avoid midday, when the asphalt heats up.

### Two Working Parents? How to Never Miss a Dog Walk or Mix Up Whose Turn It Is

URL: https://poopiemate.com/en/dual-income-dog-walk-schedule/
Published: 2026-08-27 · Updated: 2026-10-28 · Author: Jin

Use walk time reminders together with a shared family log, and you'll have fewer days with a missed walk, even when everyone is busy.

#### Common struggles for dual-income households

- Mornings are a rush before work, so it's easy to forget the walk.

- When you get home late, evening walk times end up all over the place.

- Sometimes neither partner knows who walked the dog today.

#### Basic routine tips

- Set morning and evening walk times ahead of time

- Get in the habit of checking reminders right away

- Log the walk as soon as you're back so no one else doubles up

#### When it's unclear whose turn it is

Even with a set schedule, if there's no way to confirm a walk happened, things go wrong. Everyone thinks someone else went and nobody goes. Or the dog gets walked twice. And on days when plans suddenly change, a fixed schedule alone can't keep up.

- Log it right after the walk so there's a record that it's done

- Before heading out, check the log first

- Instead of a fixed schedule, look at the day's log and take turns as needed

#### POOPIEMATE routine reminders + family sharing

#### FAQ

Q. We both work and often miss walk times. How can we manage it?

Set walk times and get reminders, and you'll forget less often.

Q. If family members walk the dog separately, can we avoid doubling up?

Yes. When one person logs a walk, the rest of the family gets notified right away, so nobody heads out for a walk that already happened.

Q. How do I keep records separate when I have several dogs?
